raw.assessment: The incumbent already delivers the intended course set in 32/40 exports, with seven-minute median handling among unchanged-assignment cases. This supports retaining the private CSV workflow while investigating change-related failures. Current-assignment semantics plausibly contribute to six affected exports, but causality is unproven. The two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only account: missing rows and unrecognized labels remain distinct possibilities. Short job runtimes cannot explain replacement delays alone. Zero observed cross-center rows excludes neither unobserved failures nor the unsampled course-split case. Any bounded change retains the next-40 target: median handling <=12 minutes, >=38 intended course sets, zero foreign-center records.

openings.claim: Export selection based on current course metadata may disagree with the intended week's roster; renames may separately make complete exports appear incomplete.
openings.delta: Distinguishes actual membership errors from recognition errors before choosing a correction.
openings.prediction: Holding fabricated attendance fixed, current-versus-week-effective selection changes row membership after reassignment; a pure recognition problem leaves membership unchanged while coordinators flag renamed labels.
openings.probe: In private staging, compare existing exports against coordinator-agreed weekly rosters for reassignment, rename, unchanged, and split-course fixtures, including two centers. Inspect membership separately from displayed labels. Keep the documented CSV schema and attendance entry available; bound this diagnostic within six engineer-days and existing hosting.
assumptions: Fabricated weekly rosters can represent the relevant transitions.
Historical metadata availability and repair cost remain unverified; staging results alone do not establish production causality.

openings.claim: Does replacement waiting create substantial active handling, or is checking and importing the dominant handling cost?
openings.delta: Separates calendar delay from the measured coordinator workload.
openings.prediction: If waiting drives active handling, prompts and repeated checks occupy appreciable time; otherwise checking, correction, or import dominate despite long delivery delays.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators' two short sessions with fabricated files to time checking, correction, download, import, and replacement follow-up separately. Reconcile available request/delivery timestamps without treating elapsed waiting as active work.
assumptions: Short sessions may undercapture multi-day follow-up; record that uncertainty.
Both probes share the same six-day resource ceiling.

raw.assessment: Synthetic observations suggest two reusable properties: short export execution and independently maintained timetables. Neither establishes a cause of missing courses. Completion logs do not establish file correctness, and zero observed cross-center rows excludes the split-course center. These are alternative bounded hypotheses, with feasibility and availability checks preceding implementation.

openings.claim: The existing export job's short execution time could support coordinator-triggered replacement exports within the private service.
openings.delta: Reuse the scheduled generator as an authorized replacement operation, reducing the delay between a corrected request and a downloadable file.
openings.prediction: If request dispatch or delivery causes much of the replacement delay, direct triggering will shorten request-to-file time without materially increasing execution time. Repeating an unchanged faulty request may leave course-set errors intact.
openings.probe: First verify that the generator accepts explicit center/week inputs and can run outside its schedule. In fabricated staging, compare queued and direct replacements using completion logs and request timestamps; exercise concurrent attendance entry and center isolation, including a split course. Estimate effort and hosting cost before selecting this change.
assumptions: The existing generator can be reused with enforced center authorization.
Concurrent runs fit the hosting allowance and six engineer-days without blocking attendance entry.

openings.claim: Can a coordinator's existing timetable supply an explicit intended course set for a requested week before export generation?
openings.delta: Reuse a document currently consulted after download as an earlier scope input, potentially avoiding dependence on current instructor assignments.
openings.prediction: If these timetables are timely and independently identify the intended courses, coordinators will resolve fabricated reassignment and rename cases before generation; stale schedules or ambiguous split-course mappings will defeat that benefit.
openings.probe: With consenting coordinators, verify timetable ownership, update timing and course identifiers against the documented CSV. Compare current checking with private pre-export course confirmation on equivalent fabricated weeks. Record intended-set accuracy and total handling time, including transcription. Include renamed, reassigned and split courses; keep the CSV schema fixed.
assumptions: An existing timetable can be mapped to authorized service courses without participant data leaving private workspaces.
Earlier confirmation saves more work than it introduces; a small implementation fits the stated budget.

openings.claim: Current metadata may misselect weekly membership; renames may impair recognition.
openings.probe: Compare current/week-effective selection against agreed fabricated rosters: reassignment, rename, unchanged and split cases across two centers; inspect labels separately.
openings.uncertainty: History availability, repair cost, fixture realism and production causality unknown.

openings.claim: Direct replacements may reduce dispatch/delivery delay; handling benefit depends on active follow-up burden.
openings.discriminator: Request-to-file latency versus active workload; execution time separately.
openings.probe: Six coordinators, two sessions each: time checking, correction, download, import and follow-up; reconcile timestamps. Verify explicit center/week and off-schedule reuse; compare queued/direct fabricated runs, concurrent attendance and isolation including splits; estimate cost.
openings.uncertainty: Sessions miss multi-day follow-up; waiting is not work. Authorization/concurrency feasibility unknown; unchanged faulty requests stay faulty.

openings.claim: Existing timetables may supply intended courses before export.
openings.discriminator: Accuracy and total handling including transcription.
openings.probe: Verify ownership, freshness and identifiers; compare current checking/private pre-export confirmation on equivalent reassigned, renamed and split weeks.
openings.uncertainty: Heterogeneous/stale timetables, ambiguous mappings and implementation cost may defeat benefit.

post_distill.decision: Diagnose before choosing. Shared ceiling: six engineer-days/existing hosting. Preserve private authorized data, CSV schema and uninterrupted attendance. Synthetic observations establish no cause; clean samples/completion logs prove neither isolation nor correctness. Next 40: median handling <=12 minutes, >=38 intended sets, zero foreign-center records.
